profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Dropbox | co-host @ Los Full Stackers podcast | he/him
profile.summary:
I’m currently a Senior Software Engineer at Dropbox, working on large-scale metadata services that power core product infrastructure. My work sits at the intersection of distributed systems, storage, and backend platform engineering — designing systems that remain reliable under massive scale and constant change.

Previously, I built backend platforms and internal tooling at Humu and Workday, helping teams ship data-driven applications and scalable services. Across these roles, I’ve worked on service architecture, APIs, developer tooling, and infrastructure that supports real-world production systems.

I studied Computer Science and Engineering at University of California, Los Angeles, where I developed a strong foundation in systems, distributed computing, and software engineering.

Technically, I’m most interested in:
	•	distributed systems and data infrastructure
	•	storage systems and metadata architectures
	•	backend platform design and APIs
	•	building tools that help developers move faster

Outside of work, I enjoy exploring new ideas at the intersection of systems, AI, and product development, and I co-host the Los Full Stackers podcast, where we discuss engineering, careers in tech, and lessons from building real systems.

Always curious about how large systems work — and how to make them simpler.

Working as a Infrastructure Engineer in Workday' UX organization to maintain and develop build integration, UI micro-services, test framework, and authentication application. Responsibilities also include cross-team collaboration with middle and back-end layers to build out new UI features, and fixing bugs reported internally and by customers.

Projects

- Designed and implemented test automation framework for front-end developers
- Deployed micro-services using WPC, an in-house platform based on OpenStack

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description: Design Test Framework Infrastructure in Java on top of Selenium Web Driver. Build up reusable library code for automating HTML5 widgets . Co-ordinate across DEV, BUILD, QA/Automation teams, ensure automation coverage & support CI process.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher, Embedded Systems
positions.description:
Worked under the supervision of distinguished Professor Majid Sarrafzadeh on the development of an FPGA-based framework for sensor-driven robotic control.
 
The research was conducted in three stages. First, we identified and integrated the peripherals required for the embedded system, studied their hardware interfaces, and determined how to access the device registers needed to acquire sensor data.
 
In the second stage, we designed and implemented an FPGA-based embedded hardware system using Xilinx Platform Studio (XPS). The system was deployed on a Digilent Genesys FPGA development board featuring a Xilinx Virtex-5 FPGA.
 
In the final stage, we integrated the embedded system with an iRobot robotic platform. Rather than relying on autonomous control, the robot was controlled through real-time input from external sensors. A gyroscope and accelerometer were used as the initial sensor inputs, with their interfaces designed as reusable components within a generalized architecture that could be extended to support additional sensors.
 
The project resulted in a modular FPGA-based framework for sensor-driven control of an iRobot platform, designed to support extensibility across multiple sensors and robotic applications.

positions.description: Worked under the supervision of Dr. Alfonso Cardenas,  for the Multimedia Information System Technology research group as a software engineer in Data Mining in the Internet and Patent Area . ● Developed a medical image viewer on the Android 3.0 platform so that physicians could have easier and remote access to patients’ medical images and records.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Designed test suite to analyze correctness of web applications made by the Spitzer Mission Operations Team.  Test suite checked for functional behavior. Implemented using Selenium and PHPUnit. Learned to automate the setup of virtual machines using Vagrant and Virtual Box.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Designed web application to track communication between spacecrafts and Deep Space Network Stations. Application also searched for specific events taking place in the communication to verify acquisition of signal. Developed parser to check for spacecraft command errors and corrupted communication settings. Parser generated summary of errors. Both software products were bought by multiple mission projects.

projects.title: Autonomous Robot: Line Following Robot
projects.description:
Designed line following robot for UCLA course Digital Design Project Laboratory. Made using
Virtex 5 Development Board, CMOS camera, and an Irobot. Worked in a team of three students.
Robot is able to recognize straight paths, dead ends, intersections, sharp turns, and curve turns; it recognized its path by keeping track of a blue colored duck tape. C code was used to program the robot; Xilinx SDK was used to run and test code. Base hardware was generated using Xilinx XPS.

projects.title: Multimedia Information Systems Technology Group
projects.description: Webmaster of research group's website. I use Javascript, HTML, Jquery, and CSS as part of the site's stack.
